title: Institutional Investment
description: What the big institutions are doing with Indian shares: foreign portfolio investors (FPIs, NSE's FIIs) from NSDL's daily record and NSE's provisional figures, domestic institutions (DIIs: mutual funds, insurers, banks, pension funds) from NSE, and both sides' index-futures positions. Linked from CAN SLIM's header.

target.queryText:
SELECT MIN(t.executed_ts) AS time,
       i.symbol || ' ' || t.side || ' ' || SUM(t.quantity) || ' @ '
         || printf('%.2f', SUM(t.quantity * t.price) / SUM(t.quantity))
         || CASE WHEN n.sentiment IS NULL THEN '' ELSE ' - ' || n.sentiment END
         || CASE WHEN n.note IS NULL THEN '' ELSE ': ' || n.note END AS text,
       t.side || COALESCE(',' || n.sentiment, '') AS tags
FROM trade_note n
JOIN trade t ON t.id = n.trade_id
JOIN instrument i ON i.id = t.instrument_id
WHERE t.side = 'BUY'
GROUP BY i.symbol, t.session_date, t.side, COALESCE(t.order_id, 'at' || t.executed_ts), n.sentiment, n.note
ORDER BY MIN(t.executed_ts)
LIMIT 500

panels.title: Net buying, ₹ crore: the latest day and the days before it
panels.description:
Each flow's purchases less sales, in rupees crore: green is net buying, red net selling. The latest day held and its date, then the sums over the last five days held, the month and the year to that day.

- **FII/FPI and DII in the cash market** are NSE's provisional figures for the trading day, published that evening from what the brokers report. NSE shows only the latest day, so these start on the first day this page was read and build up from there.
- **FPI** figures are NSDL's, the depositories' record from what the custodians report: the reporting day covers the trading day before it. They include what the exchanges' figures do not: shares bought in IPOs, placements and block deals (primary market and others), and debt. Read back two years.

Foreign selling with domestic buying absorbing it is the pattern of most of the recent years; both selling at once is when the market falls hardest.

targets.rawQueryText:
WITH names(series, name, position) AS (
  VALUES ('FII_CASH_NET', 'FII/FPI in the cash market (NSE, provisional)', 1),
         ('DII_CASH_NET', 'DII in the cash market (NSE, provisional)', 2),
         ('FPI_EQUITY', 'FPI equity, every route (NSDL)', 3),
         ('FPI_EQUITY_EXCHANGE', 'FPI equity on the exchanges (NSDL)', 4),
         ('FPI_EQUITY_PRIMARY', 'FPI equity, primary market and others (NSDL)', 5),
         ('FPI_DEBT', 'FPI debt (NSDL)', 6)),
latest AS (
  SELECT n.series, n.name, n.position, MAX(m.observed_on) AS day
  FROM names n
  JOIN market_series m ON m.series = n.series
  GROUP BY n.series, n.name, n.position)
SELECT l.name AS "Flow",
       CAST(strftime('%d', l.day) AS INTEGER) || ' '
         || substr('JanFebMarAprMayJunJulAugSepOctNovDec', (CAST(strftime('%m', l.day) AS INTEGER) - 1) * 3 + 1, 3)
         || ' ' || strftime('%Y', l.day) AS "As of",
       (SELECT ROUND(m.value) FROM market_series m WHERE m.series = l.series AND m.observed_on = l.day) AS "Latest day",
       (SELECT ROUND(SUM(v.value)) FROM (SELECT m.value FROM market_series m WHERE m.series = l.series
          ORDER BY m.observed_on DESC LIMIT 5) v) AS "Last 5 days",
       (SELECT ROUND(SUM(m.value)) FROM market_series m WHERE m.series = l.series
          AND m.observed_on >= substr(l.day, 1, 7) || '-01') AS "Month to date",
       (SELECT ROUND(SUM(m.value)) FROM market_series m WHERE m.series = l.series
          AND m.observed_on >= substr(l.day, 1, 4) || '-01-01') AS "Year to date"
FROM latest l
ORDER BY l.position

panels.title: FII and DII net buying in the cash market (₹ crore a day, NSE)
panels.description: NSE's provisional figures: each day's purchases less sales by foreign institutions (FII/FPI) and domestic ones (DII), side by side. NSE keeps only the latest day, so the bars start on the first day this page was read; a weekday the afternoon run missed stays empty.

panels.title: FPI net investment in equity a month (₹ crore, NSDL)
panels.description: NSDL's daily FPI equity figures added up by month (the current month so far): bought and sold on the exchanges, and through the primary market and other routes (IPOs, placements, block deals off the exchange), stacked. Months of selling on the exchanges while the primary market still takes money in are common: FPIs selling what they hold while buying new issues.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT CAST(strftime('%s', substr(observed_on, 1, 7) || '-01') AS INTEGER) AS time,
       ROUND(SUM(value)) AS "On the exchanges"
FROM market_series
WHERE series = 'FPI_EQUITY_EXCHANGE'
GROUP BY substr(observed_on, 1, 7)
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: FPI net investment in equity a day, and over 20 days (₹ crore, NSDL)
panels.description: Every route, a reporting day at a time (bars, left axis), and the sum of the last 20 reporting days, about a month (line, right axis). The line crossing zero is the foreign money turning.

panels.title: FPI net investment in debt a month (₹ crore, NSDL)
panels.description: NSDL's daily FPI debt figures (the general limit, the voluntary retention route and the fully accessible route, which holds the government bonds in global bond indices) added up by month. Foreign money comes into Indian bonds when the yield gap over US Treasuries is wide and the rupee steady; see Bonds and Commodities for the US side.

panels.title: Index futures: the share of each side's open contracts held long (%)
panels.description: From NSE's participant-wise open interest at each day's end: of the index futures each group holds, the share that is long. Above 50 the group is net long, below it net short. FIIs' share is the one most watched: a low and falling share is foreign money betting on a fall or hedging what it holds; clients (retail) tend to sit on the other side.

targets.rawQueryText:
SELECT CAST(strftime('%s', l.observed_on) AS INTEGER) AS time,
       ROUND(100.0 * l.value / (l.value + s.value), 1) AS "FII"
FROM market_series l
JOIN market_series s ON s.series = 'IDX_FUT_FII_SHORT' AND s.observed_on = l.observed_on
WHERE l.series = 'IDX_FUT_FII_LONG' AND l.value + s.value > 0
ORDER BY l.observed_on
